cohort: The study included 577 first-cycle patients from a single Australian IVF clinic, who were of advanced maternal age (>= 35 years) with non-male factor infertility, utilised standard IVF or ICSI insemination, and had at least three oocytes collected.
finding: Standard IVF insemination significantly increased the chance of a live birth (31%) compared with ICSI insemination (14%) in women >= 35 years with non-male factor infertility.
